# Kozmos product design gap register

A maintained requirements register for product teams and coding agents. Use it with the
[SDK coverage and implementation plan](sdk-module-primitives.md), not as an instruction to
implement every historical suggestion without checking its current criterion.

## Baseline and scope

Release reconciliation: React **0.15.2** on `latest` with `@kozmos-ds/styles` 0.15.2, icons 0.9.0, product-contracts
0.10.0 and tokens 0.8.1 (published 2026-11-07 from `c3da4baa2bae761ecc1aebd8e50ecbe94d40a92e`; the
[0.15.2 evidence](release-process.md#0152)). **Released in 0.15.2**, a patch shipped before the minors (decision 171):
"No results found" said on React (GAP-224, #484), the field-end hover and Input's pressed toggle (GAP-227, decisions
164 and 165, #487), OTPInput's first frame and its `otp_code_completed` (#490), and Combobox, MultiSelect and
FloorSelector showing a prop change in its own commit (#491); none of the items promised for 0.16.0 is in it.
**Released in 0.15.1** (published 2026-11-06 from `4cc3d04119e9f6fe5494417d0bec14cc6de8f7b6`; the
[0.15.1 evidence](release-process.md#0151)), a patch (decision 161): the web packages of Vue 3
Phase 0, `@kozmos-ds/styles`, first published, which React takes its stylesheet from and pins exactly (GAP-149), and
`@kozmos-ds/icons/vue` (GAP-148). React's exports, HTML and stylesheet are 0.15.0's, and none of the items promised
for 0.16.0 is in it. **Released in 0.15.0** (published 2026-11-04 from `08e9216c7f5440b45c1c3b9d0692b26113b05bb8`;
the [0.15.0 evidence](release-process.md#0150)): the APIs of decision 119, less Stepper's
objects, parked by decision 149 (GAP-173). Accordion's boxed form (GAP-209), Navbar's `logoInset` (GAP-208, decision
150), host actions on results and the details card (GAP-028, GAP-130), Link's `external` (GAP-202), Progress's ring
(decision 131: GAP-038's Chart family stays open), the venue icon names (GAP-105), `BuildingPresentation` and
`SitePresentation` (GAP-175) and CardTitle's headings (GAP-205) are on React with SwiftUI and Compose in the
repository. IconButton's `counter` (GAP-197), CardHeader's `actions` (GAP-169), Input's `action` (GAP-154), Navbar's
`navigationAlign` (GAP-196), Sidebar's `inset` (GAP-199), Drawer's inline `placement` (GAP-198) and Tree's `divided`
(GAP-201) are on React, with their natives in 0.16.0 (decision 134). `toast()` and `<Toaster>` (GAP-167) and
AdaptiveMapShell's `status` and top corners (GAP-123, SDK-UI-002) are React only. The Figma importer draws each part
it names; the live library takes them at the owner's next Update, which this release does not prove. Production
builds carry no component names (#447), the stylesheet lost 0.66 KB before what the release adds (#456), Notice
draws each tone's own mark (#459), and TourStep's Close leaves the flow (#458). SwiftUI's GAP-203 (#436) and the
natives' half of GAP-194 (#437) are in the repository. Each row keeps the board, Figma, native and device acceptance it
says is open. **Released in 0.14.0** (published 2026-11-01 from `5df3af1ff96e4670571564b067e33d68ac1696d5`; the
[0.14.0 evidence](release-process.md#0140)):
MAP-64's parts (decision 116): TourStep (GAP-188, and so GAP-157), Backdrop's cut-out (GAP-189), PopoverAnchor
(GAP-190), Stepper's dots (GAP-191) and option groups (GAP-192), with SwiftUI and Compose to come; GAP-193, GAP-204
and React's half of GAP-194. Their rows keep board, Figma and device acceptance open. Earlier, React 0.13.0 with the
same tokens, icons and product-contracts (published 2026-10-26 from `ba2a28f427b596d63ee069270f871f4be13dfd41`; the
[0.13.0 evidence](release-process.md#0130)), and React 0.10.0 with tokens 0.6.0, icons 0.6.0 and product-contracts 0.9.0
(published 2026-10-09 from `1ddc4d10e67616eaaa9d984ca0c3ec830c78087e`).
SwiftUI and Compose changes are available in this repository, not as newly published native
registry packages. **Released in 0.10.0**: decisions 59–69 (the theme fill, one-override
re-branding through `var()` token references (GAP-23), emotion and secondary button states, the
accent colour, the pins, GAP-45), ClientAppBanner (GAP-127), EmptyState `progress` (GAP-115),
Itinerary's Change actions (GAP-104), RouteSummary's `actions` and route preview (GAP-110, GAP-111),
`summaryLanguage` (GAP-125), the assistant in a side panel and its header inset (GAP-124, GAP-121),
credits that never clip (GAP-135), SwiftUI and Compose Container `inset` (GAP-134), and fixes up to
#266. See the [0.10.0 evidence](release-process.md#0100). **Released in 0.9.0**, after 0.8.1: navigation completion (#193), Pointr Maps -
Express wayfinding icons (#199) and walking's FollowTheLine glyph (#201), one link rule (#198), the
route waypoints' edge (#210) and the native user-location marker with the `Map marker` tokens (#211).
The Figma plugin's icon-source fix (#200) and the Figma painters ship from the repository, not npm.
A library release is not host, device or Figma acceptance. See the [release evidence](release-process.md#090) and
[maintenance checklist](design-system-maintenance.md#post-publication-documentation-checklist).

Enhancements must ship in sync across React, iOS and Android. The current component increment
adds collapsed floor-availability cues and full-name hints on all three targets, plus logical
MapOverlay start/end positions for RTL mirroring. The user confirmed keeping per-floor result
badges in lists, **off by default** behind `showResultCounts`; the closed tile never shows them.
This supersedes the historical GAP-070 request for a closed-tile count. It is no longer a defect
to omit that count. The source rows below retain its current list-only count requirement.

The released source also fixes native stale floor selection (no first-floor substitution
or fabricated stepper choices), preserves Android's existing positional formatter calls, and
corrects web compact-stepper RTL separators. This fixes the React divider defect described by GAP-086; it does not certify all RTL
behavior, native rendering or external feature boards.

The released shell foundation adds measured logical bottom-start/end slots to all three
targets, wrapping on narrow hosts and hiding the complete region when height is insufficient.
Bottom camera padding is opt-in. Compose now measures panel/top-bar/safe-area insets instead
of only echoing input; native shells no longer force a 448pt/dp minimum. React reports a
conservative combined corner envelope; native full rectangle snapshots are not implemented.

The popup follow-up now bounds long lists in registered shell corners, scrolls without shrinking
floor targets, reveals selection and dismisses when the region disappears across all three targets.
SDK-UI-001 and SDK-UI-002 remain partial: full keyboard/device acceptance, standalone/native
window edge cases, real SDK wiring, Figma mapping and consuming-board adoption still need work.
LanguageSwitcher is published for web. At 0.7.0 the owner confirmed no native language button
(iOS and Android use the device's or the app's language); decision 70 (2026-10-09) replaced that:
SwiftUI and Compose build it for iPad and other large-screen apps, and on phones the SDK hides it
(SDK-UI-003), so its native absence is a gap to close, not an exception. Actual web SDK locale
application and native runtime locale handling remain host work. The released attribution
and information components now exist across React, SwiftUI and Compose. MapInfoPanel and its
MapInfo host preserve the map/browse subtree, reserve a logical-end pane on wide screens and
open full-screen on compact/mobile hosts. The browser example includes this flow. The live
iOS Pointr QA app now adopts it: iPhone full-screen isolation and iPad pane/SDK viewport
resizing, POI retention and query retention passed simulator UI tests. A keyboard double-inset
defect found during that integration was fixed in the SwiftUI shell. Web/Android live SDK
hosts, route/floor-specific preservation and physical-device acceptance remain separate work.
Exit building is approved for 0.15.0 as a recipe, `exitBuilding()` on a MapControlButton (SDK-UI-006, decision
119).

The final layout increment makes wide search/details panels hug short content and caps long
content above the footer. Search-header top spacing matches the side spacing. Attribution
is centered on the **full map**, not the map area remaining beside a panel; symmetric corner
reservations preserve that centre. Its bottom inset matches the corner controls. If the
centred slot cannot accommodate the brand, attribution alone lifts above the controls.
Native SDK-owned attribution remains SDK-owned; the iOS QA host does not add duplicate credits.

Release-readiness review also found and reproduced a React floor menu overlapping a long
panel on the same side, while the native bounds helpers refused to open in that arrangement.
Shell-bound menus now permit horizontal displacement into the clear map region on all three
targets. Short/long panels in LTR/RTL have named browser checks; native helpers have separate
regressions for horizontal displacement and retain vertical/standalone availability guards.
These library changes are **released in React 0.7.0**, with corresponding SwiftUI/Compose
source in the release commit. Integration PR #175, security PR #174 and version PR #176 are
merged. Publication and documentation deployment are verified; none of these facts closes
host adoption, Figma mapping or physical-device acceptance by itself.

### What each status means

- **React fixed/shipped**: supported by current source, exports and/or release notes.
  Focused tests are identified below. It does not certify every native target or product board.
- **Fixed on main, not yet released**: merged to main with its tests; the row names the
  changeset the next release carries. SwiftUI and Compose are not published to a registry, so a
  native-only fix reaches a product from a checkout of main.
- **Repository work complete; external adoption unverified**: a generator/documentation output
  is present, but the external Claude Design artifact or consuming product has not been retested.
- **Partial**: useful support exists but does not satisfy the entire requirement or integration.
- **Open, source-confirmed**: the missing API or problematic implementation remains in the
  inspected source. A browser/device reproduction may still be needed before a fix.
- **Carried forward / reported shipped**: preserved evidence from the supplied document, not a
  new verification. This is deliberately different from either proven open or proven fixed.
- **Decision needed / external pending**: settle product scope or owner-controlled configuration
  before implementing. Do not replace that decision with a workaround.

A feature is complete only when its needed library API, host wiring, target-platform checks,
design mapping and named acceptance board all agree. Keep those layers separately recorded;
a React package release is not proof of native, Vue, Figma or artifact deployment.

phases 2 and 3 the screens after it.

The source rows Cloud needs as they stand: GAP-016 (the Vue package; GAP-148 is its foundation), GAP-036
(PageHeader), GAP-037 (Table's alignment and sortable headers), GAP-038 (Chart), GAP-040 (SettingsRow), GAP-041
(PublishStatus, a Dashboard module by decision 88), GAP-042 (the compact anchor list, closed as won't do by decision
154: Cloud takes NavigationItem's rows), GAP-050 (SegmentedControl's
height), GAP-098 (NumberInput's unit), GAP-106 (the persona mark), GAP-107 (Tree's meta below the name), GAP-052
(Button's dense size, which GAP-146 answers), GAP-035 (CardTitle's size), GAP-058 (sizing a Stack or Grid child),
GAP-116 (Container's vertical inset), and GAP-014 and GAP-051 (DateRangePicker's second calendar icon and its
labels).

A full-width destructive Button needs no row. Button's docs page gives full width on all three platforms
(`className="w-full"`, `fillsWidth: true`, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`), and each has a destructive variant.

GAP-188 to GAP-192 are MAP-64's: Self-Guided On-Screen Tutorials & On-Screen Hints, a Pointr Cloud feature. The
2026-10-26 export numbers them GAP-146 to GAP-150 (see Baseline and scope), so each row keeps the source's ID. Their
requirement columns are the source's, with references between them written with these IDs, apart from GAP-188's,
which say what was built (decision 136). Each was checked against
`main` (`e83161e4`) on 26 Oct, and the boards were counted from the canvas's single-file export, read as data. Targets
are the source's, the web and Figma; decision 88 builds a Core part on SwiftUI and Compose too, which for these is
the owner's call. The API each row proposes is for the owner to approve.

MAP-64's other parts need no row; each is built from Kozmos today:

- the welcome dialog ('Welcome page · Admin', '· Read-Only') is Dialog: DialogTitle, DialogDescription, a List of
  the tours (an Icon in an AvatarFallback, Text, a Tag for 'Admins', a success Tag for 'Completed', Text for
  'Paused at step 2 of 3', and a Button: Start, Replay or Resume) and a DialogFooter with a link Button ('Don't show
  again') and a secondary one ('Not now'). DialogContent is 512 wide with 24 of padding (`Dialog.tsx:67`), so its
  picture sits inside the padding, not to the edges as the wireframe draws it;
- 'Getting started' in the account menu and 'Show me how' are Menu: a MenuLabel for the email, and MenuItems whose
  children are a Text and a muted Text (MenuItem takes any children). 'Show me how' is a link Button with an Icon,
  as the MenuTrigger;
- the resume offer ('Left the page') is Toast with `duration={Infinity}`: ToastTitle, ToastDescription, two
  ToastActions and ToastClose. ToastViewport sits bottom right from 640 wide (`Toast.tsx:16`), a physical side, so
  in right to left it is at the start; GAP-099 asks for a placement;
- the failed save ('Action fails') is Alert `variant="destructive"` with `live="assertive"`, the saved states Alert
  `variant="success"` with `live="polite"`, and a step's hint line Alert `variant="info"`;
- A2's 'Client › Site › Building › Level › Feature' is Tags, the current one themed and its place also said in
  words, not by colour alone; A3's index table is Table, and 'Next tour: Level indexes' is Link.

The rest of each board is Cloud's own screens, which the 15 Oct rows and the CLOUD-UI modules cover.

GAP-193 to GAP-201 come from the 27 Oct export (see Baseline and scope): MAP-111's open Select (GAP-193), and the
rows MAP-64's redesign found on its Specs page of 19 boards on Kozmos react 0.13.0 (versions 49 to 66). Each was
checked against `main` (`2a5ceaeb`) on 28 Oct. Their requirement columns are the source's, and its other new rows
join the rows they repeat. On 27 Oct the owner approved five of them for 0.15.0 (decision 119) and left GAP-195 and
GAP-200 to decide. On the redesigned boards, four stand-ins have a Kozmos answer today:

- the icons (the source's GAP-151 and GAP-152, and the toolbar's): every glyph is a named export of
  `@kozmos-ds/icons`, drawn as `<Icon icon={HelpCircle} />` (decision 121);
- the toolbar's tools are ToggleButtons, with a pressed state, not ghost Buttons (CLOUD-UI-005);
- the shell's overrides of `--primitives-radius-button`, `-input` and `-card` do nothing, since no part reads them;
  parts read the semantic radius roles, and Cloud keeps Kozmos's 16 and 20 (decision 118);
- the map's buttons are MapControlButton as it is (decision 130, amending 96 on 28 Oct; the canvas mounts it since
  version 74), not an outline IconButton.

GAP-216 to GAP-223 come from the 2026-11-05 export (see Baseline and scope): MAP-64's and MAP-619's rows of 29 Oct
to 4 Nov that no row here held. Their requirement columns are the source's, with its references written with this
register's IDs (its GAP-209, the outlined fields, is GAP-219), apart from GAP-223's Suggested change and Done when,
which are decision 166's. GAP-219 is closed as it comes in. Each was checked against `main` (`4cc3d041`) on 6 Nov, and
each new API is the owner's to approve.

| GAP-236 | —                        | **Native fields (the error is not on the field)** (a11y). React's OTPInput puts `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` on its cells (`OTPInput.tsx:299–300`), so a screen reader says the field is in error and reads its message with it. SwiftUI's and Compose's Input, NumberInput, PasswordInput, Combobox, MultiSelect and OTPInput draw `errorMessage` as a text of its own after the field (`OTPInput.kt:290`), and the field carries no error: Compose sets no `error()` semantics, which Compose 1.6 has, and SwiftUI's label, value and hint leave it out (`OTPInput.swift:406–408`). A screen-reader user hears the error only by moving past the field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Compose sets `error(message)` on the field while it is in error; SwiftUI adds the message to the field's accessibility value, as UIKit has no invalid state. contracts (decision 88), and they keep module IDs (decision 91). A Core part a module lacks is a GAP row above,
named here rather than repeated. PublishStatus (GAP-041) is a Dashboard module too, and keeps its source ID. Each
phase ships React, the Claude Design card and the Figma painter first, then Vue (decision 84).

Repository evidence:
[FloorSelector](../packages/react/src/components/FloorSelector/FloorSelector.tsx),
[ManoeuvreCard](../packages/react/src/components/ManoeuvreCard/ManoeuvreCard.tsx),
[MapStatusPill](../packages/react/src/components/MapStatusPill/MapStatusPill.tsx),
[React changelog](../packages/react/CHANGELOG.md),
[AdaptiveMapShell](../packages/react/src/components/AdaptiveMapShell/AdaptiveMapShell.tsx),
[POIResultCard](../packages/react/src/components/POIResultCard/POIResultCard.tsx),
[POIResultList](../packages/react/src/components/POIResultList/POIResultList.tsx),
[Itinerary](../packages/react/src/components/Itinerary/Itinerary.tsx),
[contracts](../packages/product-contracts/src/index.ts),
[icon registry](../packages/icons/src/registry.ts),
[named icon artwork](../packages/icons/src/pointr/icons.generated.ts),
[native SDK screen](../apps/PointrPlayground/Sources/App/SDKMapScreen.swift),
[generated artifact documentation](claude-design/README.md).

Historical 0.6.0 baseline verification (2026-09-29; not rerun as a 0.7.0 all-gap audit):

- FloorSelector: 24 React tests passed.
- ManoeuvreCard: 17 React tests passed.
- MapStatusPill: 8 React tests passed.
- Claude Design generated-documentation suite: 10 tests passed, including typed examples.
- These focused checks ran in the installed post-release audit checkout. A path-restricted
  Git comparison first confirmed that these components, contracts, icons, generated cards
  and documentation-test sources were identical to the historical 0.6.0 baseline. Its dev-dependency
  security changes are not being counted as released product features.
- At that baseline review, no new full browser/device/Figma comparison, live SDK walkthrough, all-108-row reproduction,
  external feature canvas refresh or organization-artifact configuration was performed.
  JSDOM checks do not prove rendered geometry. Native source presence is not a simulator,
  VoiceOver or TalkBack pass.

The 0.7.0 implementation has additional named checks: the `test:map-controls` command
covers floor availability, registered corners, bounded menus, language transitions,
attribution geometry, browsing and information panels in each configured browser.
SwiftUI and Compose have matching component/layout tests and rendered references; the iOS
QA application additionally has information-panel simulator UI tests. These checks are
acceptance evidence for their own scenarios, not a reproduction of all 108 historical rows.
The exact release-merge [main CI run 36792093361](https://github.com/vodoco/kozmos-design-system/actions/runs/36792093361)
passed all 17 jobs, including both native jobs. The
[publication run 36828049714](https://github.com/vodoco/kozmos-design-system/actions/runs/36828049714)
passed; npm versions, latest tags and candidate integrity were read back, and a fresh npm
React 19 installation server-rendered a Button. The
[Pages run 36792093275](https://github.com/vodoco/kozmos-design-system/actions/runs/36792093275)
deployed the site and Storybook from the same commit; their live entry pages and Storybook
index were reachable. This is delivery evidence, not a new visual walkthrough of every story.
For future release readiness use exact candidate CI evidence; local logs and handoff
notes are not substitutes for required checks, physical assistive-technology testing,
Figma mapping or consumer adoption.

Post-release source corrections: [PR #160](https://github.com/vodoco/kozmos-design-system/pull/160)
merged at `5792335ef8056749573e37b2b400dbaf4dee2dc7`. The QA host now uses
[SDKFloorPolicy](../apps/PointrPlayground/Sources/App/SDKFloorPolicy.swift) for top-first
ordering/default selection; do not repeat the old claim that current main sorts ascending.
PRs #164/#180 cover native interactions and unhandled POI action behavior; #166/#168 cover
documentation truthfulness and generated API guidance. These merged maintenance changes
are distinct from the 0.7.0 published snapshot and do not close physical-device or external
consumer acceptance.

## Implementation queue after reconciliation

The [detailed implementation programme](sdk-module-primitives.md#product-gap-implementation-programme)
assigns every source-backlog row to a work package or explicit disposition, with dependencies,
compatibility decisions and per-package self-review gates. The table here is its high-level summary.

This is a proposed sequence, not release authorization. Each batch needs React, SwiftUI and
Compose implementation/tests where that surface exists, plus explicit accounting for absent
native surfaces. Language selection is no longer an exception: it goes native for large screens
(decision 70). Keep SDK data,
camera control, branding/provider policy and product ranking in their host adapters.

| Order | Scope                                                                                                                        | Required acceptance before closing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | **Accessibility and layout defects:** GAP-109/101 named map/itinerary regions, then GAP-085/114/121 hosted spacing.          | Reproduce arbitrary itinerary content outside a landmark, not just the built-in named Itinerary. Preserve focus restoration. Check header/no-header, grip/no-grip, short/long content, phone/desktop, RTL, safe areas and large text without double padding. Handle clearance must not be reduced accidentally.                                                                                 |
| 2     | **Criterion-blocking contracts:** GAP-093/096 instruction parts and language; GAP-021 staff-language match data.             | Agree shared contracts before APIs; retain string compatibility and locale word order. Language markup must survive into the accessible content; joining text into one aria-label alone loses per-part language. Test native AT separately. Do not confuse an unlisted staff language with a UI translation fallback.                                                                           |
| 3     | **Numbered results and pins:** GAP-119/120; preserve the completed GAP-108 number-tab foundation.                            | Confirm the new design intentionally supersedes Featured-only tabs. Cover featured results in any position, grouped rows, large numbers, translated Featured labels, RTL, selected/off-floor/disabled pins, theme contrast, branding and card-pin identity. The DS renders supplied indices; the host computes ranking and level filtering. Validate SDK sprite/overlay integration separately. |

Native Notice/AICompanionPanel are not present in the inspected component trees; plan those surfaces explicitly rather than claiming equivalent props already exist.                                                           |

### Decisions and deferred items, not automatic implementation

- **GAP-016:** public/native Vue delivery is a platform commitment; the current private React
  harness is intentional. Do not publish Vue to satisfy an imported suggestion. Decisions 76 and 83
  make that commitment: Vue 3 on Reka UI, whose foundation is GAP-148. The track started after 0.15.0
  (owner, 4 Nov, moving 1 Nov's "after 0.16.0"): Phase 0's P0.1 to P0.4 are done, and so is P0.5's first half, Vue
  in CI (#488, 7 Nov); its second half, a public package and a first `next` release, is next (GAP-148). Until then the
  package stays private, and it ships on `latest` only after the context bridge (GAP-230, decision 172).
- **GAP-043:** search dictation conflicts with the recorded no-search-microphone policy;
  AIInputBar voice conversation is not a substitute for that story. The icon artwork exists.
- **GAP-117:** the wrapper's “every mode change” promise conflicts with the button's intentional
  pressed/label-only reveal and GAP-087's decision. Clarify the desired behavior or narrow
  the promise; do not silently rewrite the tested behavior.
- **GAP-119:** the owner subsequently approved the SDK card appearance as the new default
  with migration notes and an explicit legacy option. The final tab uses the star itself as
  the Featured separator (no dot or dash), equal 16-unit outer/inner radii, 10-unit side padding
  and 1-unit vertical padding. Interior grouped tabs keep only the rounded bottom-end corner.
  Selection is pale neutral; pointer hover is 5% darker than the approved prior hover fill.
  Native expandable groups are included in this implementation slice. Source rows below
  preserve the imported request; these later decisions supersede its proposed punctuation.
- **GAP-120:** sprite assets and SDK layer/style integration are separate from the card
  implementation. The owner manages integration; do not claim live map acceptance or
  hard-code a provider's selected green into the component contract.
- **GAP-092:** no longer blocks the current Search with AI design, which uses Notice in the
  list header. Footer capability can remain optional backlog.
- **GAP-110 / GAP-111 (decision 57, 2026-10-06):** option A, a generic `actions` slot under
  RouteSummary's rail, and 111-C, the navigation layout as the route preview (End optional,
  `locationText`, Go and Details in `actions`). 111-C reinterprets GAP-111's done-when: the
  preview is RouteSummary's, not POIDetailPanel's. Built in #236, merged on 2026-10-07; not yet
  released.
- **GAP-135 (decision 58, 2026-10-06):** the attribution is never clipped into a scroll region;
  with too little room the Pointr logo gives way first and the credits keep their full height.
  The owner approved it as merged (#227, #245) on 2026-10-07 (Olcay), which settles the question
  this note left open: the logo may give way when there is no room for it, without a white-label
  configuration. `docs/sdk-module-primitives.md`'s acceptance now says so.
- **GAP-104 (owner's approval, 2026-10-07):** approved as merged (#239, Olcay): typed props,
  `onEditOrigin` and `onEditDestination`, rather than the suggested slots; the action named
  "Change", RouteLocationField's verb, rather than "Edit"; and `changeLabel` for its words.
- **Theme fill (decision 59, 2026-10-07):** prominent filled items use theme 500, the client's
  base colour set in the Pointr Cloud Dashboard (`#135BEC` in both themes), under the theme
  foreground, white in both: the filled primary Button, IconButton, FAB, SplitButton and every
  CTA drawn as one; a checked Checkbox and Switch, Radio's dot, a selected Chip, the default Tag
  and Badge, the brand Counter, FloorSelector's selected tile and result count, a filled
  LocationPin, SaveLocationCard's saved disc, CategoryField's count pill, the Stepper's completed
  step, ToggleButton on, ManoeuvreCard's theme appearance, the UserMessage bubble and
  POIResultCard's selected number tab. A count on the fill inverts, the theme foreground with a
  500 number: FloorSelector's on its selected tile and a default Badge's counter. The button's
  hover and focus are `#1051E8` and pressed `#0D44C2` in both themes, drawn on every platform.
  Theme text, icons, borders and focus rings on a surface use theme 600 (`#1051E8` light,
  `#5887F3` dark), and the natives moved theirs from 500 to 600, CategoryField's and
  CategoryTile's accent included. Slider, Progress and RouteProgressRail stay 600; Menu, Select
  and Listbox rows and FloorSelector's user-level dot are unchanged; React's Rating thumb is the
  theme's tint ringed in 600, as the natives and Figma draw it. The date pickers' selected day is
  the platform picker's own on React, SwiftUI and Compose, the app's accent colour (owner, 7
  Oct); only Figma draws one, in the theme fill. A client's colour reaches every fill on the web
  through one override of theme 500 (GAP-23 fixed); SwiftUI and Compose have no runtime
  override yet, so the fill there is Pointr's `#135BEC`. The owner's rulings on the PR (7 Oct):
  500 on a raised dark sheet (2.32:1 on background/200) is accepted, since each state is told by
  its mark at 5.62:1; danger and alert fills keep black ink in the dark (the dark danger fill
  reads 6.19:1 with black, 3.39:1 with white); Figma's selected NavigationItem label moves from
  700 to 600 and its Avatar image placeholder is neutral; the filled pin's ring stays
  foreground/1000; SwiftUI's `onEmphasis` tone becomes the theme foreground and a new `onDanger`
  keeps the danger fill's ink. Nothing is open any more: LocationPin `accent` parity was settled
  by decision 62, and the selected tab indicator by decision 65.
- **Emotion button states (decision 60, 2026-10-08):** a filled emotion Button's hover is one
  step and its pressed two steps further along the emotion's own ramp, away from the page:
  darker in light, lighter in dark. Its focus is its hover. Each state is a reference to its
  ramp step, so a ramp's override carries it. The light danger hover had been danger 600,
  lighter than the fill; it is now danger 800 (`#8C132B`), and pressed is 900 (`#670E20`).
  - In the dark every emotion now steps lighter: danger `#EE7E95` → `#F3A2B3` → `#F8C6D0`,
    and success, alert and informative 700 → 800 → 900, all under black.
  - The light neutral is background 200 → 300 → 400 (`#9095A2` pressed, black 7.01:1). It
    had pressed lighter, at `#E3E4E8`.
  - Exceptions: the dark neutral keeps darkening, background 300 → 200 → 100 (`#464A53` →
    `#2E3138` → `#17191C`), because white, its ink, reads 3.72:1 on the lighter step. Pressed
    is the dark sheet's own colour, which the owner accepted: the white label reads 17.6:1.
    The themed Button keeps decision 59's values.
  - Informative's ramp already existed (`emotional.info`). Light success and alert already
    followed the rule.
  - `tokens:contrast:check` holds each state to its ramp step and its direction.
- **Secondary is the neutral fill (decision 61, 2026-10-08):** the secondary Button draws the
  neutral Primary Buttons tokens in every state, with their ink, on every platform.
  - React gains hover, focus and pressed. Its dark fill moves from `#2E3138` to `#464A53`.
  - SwiftUI's words move from foreground/100 to the token's ink. Compose already matched.
  - Figma's Secondary binds the neutral tokens, so Secondary/Disabled is now the charcoal disabled
    token like Default's. That route is still DS ask 16's open question.
  - On the neutral fill, the focus ring's page-coloured gap reads only 2.19:1 (light) and 1.61:1
    (dark) against the fill, so the ring itself carries the 3:1.
- **Brand variant 1's 500 (decision 63, 2026-10-08):** `#4135F1`, lightened from `#4134F1`
  just enough to read 3:1 as a shape on the dark page (3.00:1; it was 2.99:1). The hue is
  kept, and white on it reads 6.99:1. On the dark sheet it reads 2.52:1, which is accepted as
  the theme fill's 2.32:1 is; `#4947FB` would have reached 3:1 there too and was declined. The
  contrast contract now holds variant 1's 500 to 3:1 on the page and white on it to 4.5:1.
- **Pins follow the natives (decision 62, 2026-10-08):** a featured LocationPin is the SDK's
  Featured amber, alert 500 (`#FAB735` in both themes), with its number in the alert's on-fill
  colour, black (11.89:1), whatever its variant or tint, on the web, SwiftUI, Compose and Figma.
  - React drew its variant's colour with a star badge. The star is gone (owner, 8 Oct), and
    React's accessible name adds the new `featuredLabel` ("Featured") to `label`, as the natives
    add "Featured".
  - Figma drew alert 900 under white.
  - The accent pin is brand variant 1's 500 (`#4135F1`) with a white number, and at rest its
    ring and number are the variant's 700. React drew theme 600 under foreground/1000, black in
    the dark.
  - `check-theme-fill.mjs` reads both pins in three engines, and `figma:painters:check` reads
    Figma's featured pin.
- **iOS SplitButton's menu press (decision 64, 2026-10-08):** the menu half keeps SwiftUI's system
  press, a deliberate platform difference. It is a `Menu`, which does not run a custom button
  style's pressed state. The action half draws the themed pressed token (`#0D44C2`) on every
  platform, and the menu half does so on the web and in Compose. `KozmosThemeFillPressTests` reads
  the action half for that reason.
- **Tabs (decision 65, 2026-10-08):** React's raised segment on every platform. The active tab
  is background/0, raised, with foreground/0 words, in a background/100 track, and nothing on
  tabs is the theme's colour.
  - SwiftUI and Compose dropped their theme-500 underline and bar.
  - Figma's active tab gained the raised effect it lacked.
  - The native track is 44 tall, the touch target; React's list is 40.
  - Pixel tests on both natives fail on the old underline and pass now.
- **Secondary pin (decision 66, 2026-10-08):** React's filled secondary LocationPin is
  foreground/400 under foreground/1000 (6.10:1 light, 7.76:1 dark), as SwiftUI and Compose draw
  it. It was background/200, 1.6:1 against the page.
- **`featuredLabel` on the natives (decision 67, 2026-10-08):** SwiftUI's and Compose's
  `KozmosLocationPin` take `featuredLabel` (default "Featured") for the accessible description, as
  React's `featuredLabel` does. They hard-coded English.
- **The accent colour (decision 68, 2026-10-08):** Pointr's API has a configurable accent beside
  the theme, background, foreground and emotional colours, and Kozmos now has one.
  - `Primitives.Colors.accent` is a 0–1000 ramp like theme's, with 500 as the base: `#FAB735` in
    both themes by default, the other steps the alert ramp's.
  - `Semantics.Accent.fill` (accent 500) and `Semantics.Accent.onFill` (its ink, black by default)
    are what parts draw. A product that sets its accent sets both, as the theme fill comes with the
    theme foreground.
  - **The Featured tag consumes the accent everywhere in the UI:** POIResultCard's Featured tab
    and the featured card's edge, on the web, SwiftUI, Compose and Figma. They were the alert fill
    pair (`#F9A707` / `#FBC459`), and Figma's was a grey badge.
  - **A featured pin** is the accent fill. It shows the place's logo, and without one a star where
    the number would be; it never shows its number. This brings back the star for the no-logo
    case: the owner had already added that fallback. The natives gain a marker-content slot for
    the logo.
  - `variant="accent"` on LocationPin stays brand variant 1, and Tailwind's internal `accent` role
    stays theme 600. The names are documented, not renamed (owner, 8 Oct).
  - `check-token-references.mjs` re-brands accent 500 and reads the pin, the tab and the edge.
- **GAP-45 fixed (decision 69, 2026-10-08):** brand variant 1's dark 600 is `#716EFF`, with the
  same hue: 5.38:1 on the dark page and 4.51:1 on the dark sheet, where `#6258F3` read 4.21:1 and
  3.53:1. The contract holds variant 1's 600 as text on both.
- **Every component on every platform (decision 70, owner, 2026-10-09).** The iOS and Android SDKs
  already ship an AI assistant, built without Kozmos parts. Kozmos makes every component available on
  React, SwiftUI and Compose consistently; a platform gap is closed, or kept only as a decided
  exception, never left as "not yet". At 0.10.0, 111 of 120 components are on all three. The nine
  to build:
  - the assistant family, ActionCard, AICompanionPanel, AIInputBar, AIMessage, AIMessageList,
    Notice and UserMessage, on both natives;
  - LanguageSwitcher on both natives, for iPad and other large-screen apps (on phones the SDK hides
    it, which is the product's choice);
  - Surface as a SwiftUI view (SwiftUI has the `kozmosSurface(_:style:)` modifier).
  - The assistant family starts in Figma, painted by the plugin, so all three follow one drawing.
    Then a first native step (the panel, the thread, both messages, a text-only input bar and
    Notice), then ActionCard, then voice (decision 37). The SDK teams' shipped assistant screens
    are read first, so Kozmos matches what users see and the SDKs can adopt it. No date is promised
    before that first step shows the size (P07 in the [SDK module plan](sdk-module-primitives.md)).
- **Decisions 71–73 (owner, 2026-10-14, recorded in the 14 Oct Gaps export):**
  - **71, the SDK's markers (GAP-120):** keep today's SDK markers, and Kozmos matches them: a numbered
    circle rather than a teardrop, a green pin for a place on its own (its details open), the featured
    place's logo in a rounded tile with a dark rim, and a double tap on a marker opens the place's details
    rather than zooming the map. This changes decision 68's accent-filled featured pin; how the accent
    still shows on that tile is to settle when it is built.
  - **72, double tap opens details (GAP-143, GAP-144):** a double tap on a result, open or closed, a
    group's branch included, opens its details through a new `POIResultList.onOpen`, fired once, not as
    two selections; on mobile web the list never zooms the page on a double tap.
  - **73, the assistant's close button (GAP-145):** AICompanionPanel's close is POIDetailPanel's
    IconButton (outline, neutral, rounded square) on every platform.
- **Decisions 74–78 (owner, 2026-10-14, planning and building Track 1):**
  - **74, the drag indicator (GAP-140):** about 4 above the card's edge (the source says 6), keeping the
    44pt/48dp target; on the theme fill at about 60%, built as 62% because 60% reads 2.99:1 on `#135BEC`
    and 62% reads 3.09:1. The background card's grey bar is unchanged. Tightened the same day (owner): the
    closed card ends 21 under its instruction, and the bar's target reaches up over the
    instruction's foot (which opens the card too), so the target stays 44pt/48dp without adding
    height. Open, the itinerary stops 44pt/48dp above the edge, outside what scrolls, so the target
    covers no row at any scroll position.
  - **75, scrollbars on a phone (GAP-138):** the phone presentations (the sheet, the direction card's
    itinerary, the level list) never draw a lasting scrollbar, by default, with no prop; beside the map
    and alone they draw Kozmos's thin one (GAP-139).
  - **76, a real `@kozmos-ds/vue`:** plan Vue work for the Cloud Dashboard (the 13 Vue rows), rather than
    marking them not planned. Native Vue 3 on Reka UI is recommended over wrapping React; scope, versions
    and adoption are the owner's to settle first. Settled on 15 Oct by decisions 83 and 84.
  - **77, the language menu (GAP-122):** it opens straight above its trigger, over the side panel and
    anything else, as the Web SDK's does; a long list stays above and scrolls. This reverses the earlier
    tested rule that it clear the side panel.
  - **78, CJK category names (GAP-010):** a name in Han, kana or Hangul gets a third line in a category
    tile; other scripts keep two.
- **Decisions 79–81 (owner, 2026-10-15, building Track 2 from the MAP-474 boards' marker SVGs):**
  - **79, LocationPin is the SDK's markers (GAP-120):** LocationPin draws a result's number in a pill on a
    pointer (a dot without one), a featured place's logo in a rounded tile on a dot, and a place on its own
    (its details open) as the green pin; a double tap opens the place's details (`onOpen`). Its teardrop
    variants, category tints and sizes are removed on all three platforms. `label` is the marker's whole
    accessible name, the number included, as the product writes it; Kozmos adds only `featuredLabel`
    (owner, 15 Oct). Settled on 16 Oct:
    - **Enter on the web** opens a pin that is already the current one (selected, or a place), with a
      hint in its description ("Press Enter to open details", `openHint`); otherwise Enter presses.
    - **The label beside a pin** is Semibold 600 on every platform. Figma draws it Medium, under its
      three-weight convention.
    - **`left` and `right` labels are physical** on every platform: products place them with MapLibre
      (GL and Native), which places a symbol's text by the map's left and right.
  - **80, no other-level marker:** the dashed `offFloor` state is removed; only results on the level in
    view are marked, and the level switcher counts the rest.
  - **81, markers are sprites in a product:** every marker comes from the map style's sprite sheet, and a
    featured tile with its logo from the featured sprite Pointr's back end generates; Kozmos draws the same
    for prototypes and boards. The featured tile has no accent colour (a static sprite plus the logo).
- **Decisions 82–89 (owner, 2026-10-15, the Vue and Cloud plan; reworded with the owner's answers of 16 Oct):**
  - **82, compact density for the web:** `ThemeProvider density="compact"` sizes the controls for a
    pointer-first desktop tool such as Pointr Cloud: buttons 32, 40 and 48, icon buttons 28, 32 and 40,
    single-line fields 40, with chips, rows, tabs, the table and the tree to follow (GAP-146). Touch, the
    default, keeps every size, except Badge, which moves to Chip's scale (decision 93). Web only; SwiftUI
    and Compose stay touch. `DensityScope` puts one region at another density (#274, released in React 0.12.0). On 16 Oct:
    - a compact removable chip keeps a 24 × 24 remove target, which overhangs it (decision 94);
    - SegmentedControl and OTPInput get their own density steps, after #274;
    - Figma's library gets Touch and Compact Density modes, which the painters bind to;
    - a part with its own density prop (Tree, List, NavigationItem, Timeline, BottomNavigation, and Card's
      `padding`) follows the page's density unless the prop is set.
  - **83, `@kozmos-ds/vue` is Vue 3 on Reka UI, with no UI kit:** Kozmos draws every part itself, as
    React does on Radix, and depends on no Vuetify or other component library. This settles decision
    76's scope. Vue 2 isn't supported.
  - **84, Claude Design first:** the owner designs Cloud's coming work in Claude Design with Kozmos;
    Cloud matches those designs and uses `@kozmos-ds/vue` once it has migrated. When and how Cloud
    migrates is the Cloud team's. So each phase ships React, the Claude Design cards and the Figma
    painters first, then the Vue port of the same parts. A Core variant also gets its SwiftUI and
    Compose step (decision 88).
  - **85, Maps editing first:** the first phase is what the map content panels and the add and edit
    panels need: the Core variants and the Dashboard modules marked phase 1 in their tables.
  - **86, icons:** the UI's icons are Kozmos's (the Pointr Icon Library). A type's icon keeps coming
    from the published taxonomy sprite (decision 81's rule), drawn by `SpriteIcon`, a Core part on
    every platform (16 Oct; GAP-150).
  - **87, Readex Pro stays Cloud's font:** Kozmos still ships no font. A Cloud page or a Claude Design
    prototype loads Readex Pro and points the system role at the brand family token. Claude Design's
    README says how (#276, `c7fe6abb`).
  - **88, where Cloud's parts are built (16 Oct):** a Core variant Cloud needs is built on every
    platform: React, SwiftUI, Compose, Vue and Figma. This extends decision 70, which names React,
    SwiftUI and Compose. A Dashboard module (the CLOUD-UI rows, and PublishStatus, GAP-041) is web:
    React, Vue and Figma, with a platform-neutral contract, so a native port would need no redesign. No
    iOS or Android app is planned for Cloud now ("we could build one day"). For Dashboard modules only,
    this is a decided exception to decision 70, not a "not yet".
  - **89, SDK parts stay touch under any density (confirmed 16 Oct):** an SDK screen in a compact page
    draws as the apps draw it. Every SDK part's root is a touch `DensityScope`, and its slots stay touch:
    a product's own content in one is touch too, unless the product wraps it in
    `DensityScope density="compact"`.
- **Decisions 90–97 (owner, 2026-10-16, answers on the Cloud plan):**

  - **91, IDs:** Core parts are universal. A gap in a Core part is a GAP row: GAP-146 onwards are

  - **93, Badge is a status badge:** on Chip's scale, 28, 32 and 36 at touch and 20, 24 and 28 compact,
    with no hover states, in its own PR (GAP-147). The touch Badge changes from 44. Tag has no size

  - **94, the compact removable chip:** 20 tall. Its remove button keeps a 24 × 24 target, which
    overhangs the chip.
  - **95, `@kozmos-ds/styles`:** a new public package carries the shared stylesheet, and
    `@kozmos-ds/react` re-exports it (GAP-149).
  - **96, Cloud's level and building picker and its layers button:** Dashboard modules built from Core

  - **97, the stylesheet may cost 32 KB (16 Oct):** Track 2 (#273) and compact density (#274) together
    measure 30.63 KB against 30.5: the SDK's markers in owned CSS and the density rules, both new rules.
    The owner chose 32 over 31 to leave room for the next density groups.
- **Decisions 98–115 (owner, 2026-10-21, answers on the 20–21 Oct work):**
  - **98, CI's Xcode is pinned:** `iOS Build` runs on `macos-26` with Xcode 26.6, named rather than
    `macos-latest`. A non-required workflow runs the iOS tests on the newest Xcode every week, and the
    tests Xcode 27.1 fails are fixed before the pin moves (#337).
  - **99, CI on `main` is never cancelled:** a pull request's run gives way to its newer push; every
    commit on `main` gets a finished run to release from (#337).
  - **100, label defaults:** an English default on a label parameter is the convention (Dialog's
    `closeLabel = "Close"`); a word with no parameter is a gap (GAP-182). The Android date and time
    pickers keep `"Select Date"` and `"Select Time"` as their defaults (#316, #319).
  - **101, a POI tag's broken artwork:** an unsafe or failed `iconUrl` falls back to the tag's
    `iconName` on all three platforms, as Compose did (GAP-178).
  - **102, map corners:** a framed MapView has the control radius, 16, everywhere; a map that is the
    canvas has no corners; map controls are 16 (GAP-184, #338). Figma follows the built parts.
  - **103, headings and text size:** SwiftUI's headings grow with Dynamic Type along the curve of
    their nearest system text style (#331), not by React's single rem factor.
  - **104, date and time pickers, the mix:** the web gets Kozmos's own calendar, range and time
    panels (GAP-186). iOS and Android keep the system pickers, their platform convention, inside
    Kozmos fields, in the locale's formats (GAP-183). Figma shows which open state each platform
    uses.
  - **105, typing a date on the web:** the browser's segmented typing stays, and Kozmos's calendar
    opens from the field's button (the browser's own button hidden, Firefox included). Firefox's
    cannot be hidden by a page (#352), so decision 108 keeps it there.
  - **106, Android's pickers:** Material 3's date, range and time pickers replace the framework
    dialogs, so Kozmos's theme colours them and a range is one picker (API change).
  - **107, an alert's variant:** it colours the icon, the title and the description on every
    platform, and a default description is full ink, as Figma and React draw it (#330).
  - **108, Firefox's date input:** Firefox keeps its own date button and picker until it can hide
    them (Mozilla's webcompat bug 2048623, which waits on platform bug 2051201, support for
    `::-webkit-calendar-picker-indicator`); Chromium and WebKit open Kozmos's calendar. Firefox
    switches later with no API change (#352).
  - **109, closed days:** a day out of bounds or closed keeps the muted look of another month's
    day (foreground/400), with no mark of its own.
  - **110, tooltip sides:** physical, as React's Radix and Figma's Top/Right/Bottom/Left, on
    SwiftUI and Compose too, with new `.leading`/`.trailing` cases for logical placement (API).
  - **111, WayfindingCard's close:** "Close navigation" by default on all three (`closeLabel`, #345).
  - **112, FileUpload's Code Connect:** Figma's web "Browse Text" is not mapped into native code,
    which keeps "Tap to upload file" (#357).
  - **113, a native symbol button's word:** with no label passed, it keeps the system's translated
    name for its symbol where that name is the right word (SwiftUI POICard's close, "Close" or
    "Schließen", `closeLabel: String? = nil`), and an English default where the symbol's name is
    the wrong word (FileUpload's remove, "Remove"). It refines decision 100.
  - **114, the whole library may cost 92 KB:** the budget moves from 88 to 92 KB for the web's date
    and time panels (decision 104), which take it to about 87.93 KB on CI with no lossless trim.
    The per-export, Button and stylesheet budgets are unchanged.
  - **115, list rows:** Combobox's, Select's and TimePicker's rows are 44 tall with a light active
    row, as Figma draws them, not 36 with a filled one.
- **Decisions 116–117 (owner, 2026-10-26, MAP-64 Tutorials & Hints):**
  - **116, MAP-64's five parts are approved as API:** Backdrop lights a target through a cut-out
    (GAP-189, #408), a popover the product opens beside any element or rect, `PopoverAnchor` (GAP-190,

    and Figma's Effect/glass has the opacity and no colour, so no colour token holds the white. The Vue themes and
    token-references suites (#488) hold every painted colour to a theme token and accept exactly this case, named
    `GLASS_EDGE` in `scripts/vue/in-page.mjs`: a border colour of an element with `.kozmos-button-glass` or
    `.kozmos-surface-glass`, white, at the alpha the opacity token computes to on that element, and following the
    token when it alone is set to a sentinel. A white written in at that alpha fails, and so does the allowance when
    no story uses it. There is no token and no visual change now: GAP-229 records the missing colour token,
    deferred to design, and the allowance goes when design adds one.
  - **168, the Vue bridge's listener rule (7 Nov):** a listener on a bridged wrapper goes to the React part alone
    when the part takes its `onX`, as React's types say (read into the generated `part-takes.ts`), so the part's own
    gating holds. Any other listener is a native listener on the wrapper's own element, Vue's fallthrough: it hears
    what the part draws in place and nothing it draws in a portal, as a component's listener never hears what it
    teleports. An event that does not bubble is heard from content drawn in place through the capture phase. #489
    built it.

### Source inspection and focused checks for this intake

New/current findings above were inspected against the main baseline, including:

- [Shell layout](../packages/react/src/components/AdaptiveMapShell/AdaptiveMapShell.tsx),
  [SwiftUI shell](../packages/ios/Sources/Components/AdaptiveMapShell/AdaptiveMapShell.swift)
  and [Compose shell](../packages/android/src/main/java/com/kozmos/components/AdaptiveMapShell/AdaptiveMapShell.kt):
  distinguish outer search padding, header-to-content gap and gripless-sheet top inset.
- [Notice](../packages/react/src/components/Notice/Notice.tsx) and
  [assistant panel](../packages/react/src/components/AICompanionPanel/AICompanionPanel.tsx):
  icon fallback/wrapper, header padding and missing native counterparts.
- [Result tabs](../packages/react/src/components/POIResultCard/POIResultCard.tsx),
  [owned tab CSS](../packages/styles/src/styles/owned-components.css),
  [SwiftUI tabs](../packages/ios/Sources/Components/POIResultCard/POIResultCard.swift),
  [Compose tabs](../packages/android/src/main/java/com/kozmos/components/POIResultCard/POIResultCard.kt)
  and [LocationPin](../packages/react/src/components/LocationPin/LocationPin.tsx):
  existing Featured precedence and numbered-marker appearance.
- [MapControlButton](../packages/react/src/components/MapControlButton/MapControlButton.tsx)
  and [MapControlsGroup](../packages/react/src/components/MapControlsGroup/MapControlsGroup.tsx):
  reveal key and differing public descriptions.
- [RouteSummary](../packages/react/src/components/RouteSummary/RouteSummary.tsx),
  [POIDetailPanel](../packages/react/src/components/POIDetailPanel/POIDetailPanel.tsx),
  [DirectionStep](../packages/react/src/components/DirectionStep/DirectionStep.tsx),
  [EmptyState](../packages/react/src/components/EmptyState/EmptyState.tsx) and
  [Container](../packages/react/src/components/Container/Container.tsx): API limitations in
  GAP-110–116. The existing `details` prop is POI data, not an itinerary slot.

Focused existing React suites passed **145 tests in seven files**: FloorSelector 34,
ManoeuvreCard 17, MapControlButton 14, MapControlsGroup 28, Notice 7, POIResultCard 32 and
LocationPin 13. Reproduce from the repository root with:

```bash
pnpm --filter @kozmos-ds/react exec vitest run \
  src/components/FloorSelector/FloorSelector.test.tsx \
  src/components/ManoeuvreCard/ManoeuvreCard.test.tsx \
  src/components/MapControlButton/MapControlButton.test.tsx \
  src/components/MapControlsGroup/MapControlsGroup.test.tsx \
  src/components/Notice/Notice.test.tsx \
  src/components/POIResultCard/POIResultCard.test.tsx \
  src/components/LocationPin/LocationPin.test.tsx
```

These tests confirm the existing baseline, including behaviors the new design wants to change;
they are **not failing-first reproductions of every reported gap**. No new browser geometry,
physical-device AT, native test run, canvas regeneration, Figma inspection or release was
performed for this documentation intake. Claims of missing APIs are source findings; the
source's pixel measurements and external-board axe reports remain reported evidence until
their fixtures are reproduced.

brought forward 4 Nov). Phase 0's P0.1 to P0.4 are done (#474, #475, #478, #479; GAP-148), `@kozmos-ds/styles` and `@kozmos-ds/icons/vue` released in 0.15.1 (6 Nov), and P0.5's first half, Vue in CI, is on main (#488, 7 Nov): a Vue job, required since 7 Nov, four browser suites over the Vue Storybook, Vue visual baselines and a bundle budget. Its second half, the package made public and a first `next` release, is next, and `latest` waits for the context bridge (GAP-230, decision 172). Open — `@kozmos-ds/vue` is private: its main entry is native Vue on Reka UI for ThemeProvider, DensityScope and Button (#478, GAP-148), and every other part is the React harness, now `@kozmos-ds/vue/react-bridge`. A product/platform decision, not a missing CSS adjustment. The harness cannot draw a part made of parts (mounted 17 Oct): each wrapper is its own React root, so a `KozmosRadioGroupItem` inside a `KozmosRadioGroup` throws; `KozmosToast` and `KozmosTooltip` throw without the providers it lacks; it wraps no part of Accordion, Card, Dialog, Drawer, Select, Toast or Tooltip below the root, and has no `toast()`; and `KozmosAlert` has no icon slot. Since 7 Nov (#489) `v-model` reaches React through the models each wrapper names, React's prop and its change callback, one for each controlled pair its part has. Before, it did nothing on the 21 wrappers that declared `update:modelValue`; elsewhere a guess served `v-model:checked`, `v-model:open`, and the `v-model` of a part that reports `onValueChange` (SegmentedControl, and Tabs, Select or Accordion given React's own items). A listener reaches the React part when the part takes its prop, which React's types decide (`part-takes.ts`), so the part decides what runs it; any other is a native listener on the wrapper's own element, which hears what the part draws in place and, as a component's listener never hears what it teleports, nothing it draws in a portal. Decision 168 (7 Nov) makes this the rule. The docs' Vue tabs say so, and `pnpm docs:snippets:vue:check` holds their imports to its exports. MAP-64 joined it in the 2026-10-26 export, with the parts its tours use. The 2026-10-26 export named a RadioGroup that no MAP-64 board drew; the 27 Oct export's list, from the rebuilt boards, no longer does. Its TourStep is GAP-188 here (the source's GAP-146). The 2026-11-05 export adds MAP-619, every board of which is a React stand-in, and the requirement columns here are now that export's, with the 2026-10-28 export's list of the parts MAP-64's boards use (version 72), which the 28 Oct intake recorded and this row had missed. |

Today's SDK draws result markers from its map style's sprite: a circle with the result's number, blue outline at rest, filled when selected, and a place on its own (its details open) as a green teardrop pin with a white disc and a dot where it stands, no number, the only marker; the same for search and Quick Access (decided 1 Oct, Olcay: search numbered too). So the boards draw the SDK's marker themselves (a button with Kozmos tokens): numbered blue-outline circles at rest, filled when selected, a place on its own a green pin (smaller than the SDK's) with an empty white disc, only results on the level in view marked (the level switcher counts the rest, showResultCounts). A featured place is just its logo in a rounded tile with a dark rim and a dot, no star or number, as today's SDK draws it; Kozmos's featured LocationPin adds a star badge, so the boards draw this too. Decided 14 Oct (Olcay): keep today's SDK markers; Kozmos matches them. What 0.10.0's LocationPin still draws differently: (1) a teardrop where the SDK draws a numbered circle; (2) no green pin for a place on its own (its details open); (3) the featured pin's logo in the accent amber where the SDK draws the logo in a rounded tile with a dark rim; ## Closing and maintaining a row

1. Reproduce the named criterion on the actual consumer/version; review any external build kit
   before running its commands. An attachment's shell snippet is not execution authorization.
2. Record the failing automated test and target, implement in the supported component/contract
   or host adapter, and prove that test now passes. Use a real browser/device for geometry,
   focus, keyboard avoidance and map interactions.
3. Update each required target separately: React, consuming app, iOS, Android, Figma and
   external design artifact as applicable. Vue is not currently a public native package.
4. Record the merged PR, released package/version, test names, and named acceptance board.
   Keep an external-deployment field pending until the external consumer has actually adopted it.
5. Coordinate the original feature change list; retain the ID and original criterion. Remove
   a product stand-in only after the real component passes the criterion.
6. Do not mark every target closed because a file, story, package export or passing CI job exists.
   Do not edit generated status/API-card files by hand; follow [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).

Suggested per-row closure evidence: **owner · target · merged PR · version · named test ·
consumer/board · external adoption · remaining limitation**. Keep this register focused on
requirements and durable evidence; session logs belong in the ignored `.notes/` directory.
